proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the branch \(W=\varnothing\), and suppose that \(\Pi\) entails
\[
P_M(V=v)>0\qquad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{i\in V}\Omega_i.
\tag{1}
\]
Write \(\mathcal G\) for the latent projection of \(G\) onto \(V\), and write
\[
c_0:=\operatorname{ID}(Y,X,P_M(V),\mathcal G)
\]
for the original ordinary-ID call. We prove the asserted compiler result as a universal implication, without assuming that the open latent-lifting construction exists.

Let
\[
\mathfrak A=(\Sigma,\Rightarrow,\operatorname{Comp},\iota,\rho)
\]
be an arbitrary restricted grammar instance satisfying the local classical-ID interface required in \(\mathrm{oeq:latent\text{-}lifting}\). Thus \(\Sigma\) is its state set, \(\Rightarrow\) its production relation, \(\operatorname{Comp}\) its successful compiler, \(\iota\) maps a grammar state to an ordinary call
\[
\iota(\sigma)=c(\sigma)=\operatorname{ID}(Y_c,X_c,Q_c,\mathcal G_c),
\]
and \(\rho(\sigma)\) records the map from this call back to \(c_0\). The local interface consists of the following premises.

First, there is an initial state \(\sigma_0\) with \(\iota(\sigma_0)=c_0\) and identity provenance. At every state, exactly the production matching the first applicable one of the seven ordered ID cases is available, with the same side condition. Cases \((2)\), \((3)\), and \((7)\) have the specified unique child; case \((4)\) has exactly one child for each district; cases \((1)\), \((5)\), and \((6)\) are terminal. No support-specific or functional production is available. For every recursive child \(\sigma'\), if \(\kappa_{c\leftarrow c'}\) denotes its ordinary-call provenance into its parent, then
\[
\rho(\sigma')=\rho(\sigma)\circ\kappa_{c\leftarrow c'}.
\tag{2}
\]
Failures propagate through recursive productions without changing the case-\((5)\) payload, except for the provenance composition in \((2)\).

Second, on a successful subtree the compiler obeys the following local equations. In case \((1)\),
\[
\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma)=\sum_{V_c\setminus Y_c}Q_c.
\tag{3}
\]
In case \((2)\), for the child \(\sigma_2\) embedding
\[
\operatorname{ID}\!\left(Y_c,X_c\cap A_c,
\sum_{V_c\setminus A_c}Q_c,\mathcal G_c[A_c]\right),
\]
the recursive-substitution equation is
\[
\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma_2).
\tag{4}
\]
In case \((3)\), for the child \(\sigma_3\) embedding \(\operatorname{ID}(Y_c,X_c\cup Z_c,Q_c,\mathcal G_c)\),
\[
\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma_3).
\tag{5}
\]
In case \((4)\), if \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) are the districts and \(\sigma_{4,j}\) embeds \(\operatorname{ID}(S_j,V_c\setminus S_j,Q_c,\mathcal G_c)\), then
\[
\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma)=
\sum_{V_c\setminus(Y_c\cup X_c)}
\prod_{j=1}^k\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma_{4,j}).
\tag{6}
\]
In case \((6)\),
\[
\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma)=
\sum_{S\setminus Y_c}
\prod_{i:V_i\in S}Q_c(V_i\mid V_c^{(i-1)}).
\tag{7}
\]
In case \((7)\), if \(S'\) is the unique containing district, define
\[
Q'_c:=\prod_{i:V_i\in S'}Q_c(V_i\mid V_c^{(i-1)}),
\]
and let \(\sigma_7\) embed \(\operatorname{ID}(Y_c,X_c\cap S',Q'_c,\mathcal G_c[S'])\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma_7).
\tag{8}
\]
The case-\((5)\) production emits the actual call \(c(\sigma)\), the pair \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal G_c,\mathcal G_c[S])\), and \(\rho(\sigma)\); its locally checkable payload contains the two forest subgraphs forming the relevant hedge for that failed query or subquery. Finally, the stipulated algebraic normalization map \(\mathcal N\) respects the finite sum, product, marginalization, Q-factor, and recursive-substitution operations in \((3)\)--\((8)\). These are hypotheses on the arbitrary instance \(\mathfrak A\), not an assertion that a concrete instance has been constructed.

We first discharge denominator guards rather than building positivity into the desired conclusion. If a finite kernel \(Q_c\) is strictly positive pointwise, then every one of its nonempty marginals is positive: for any fixed partial assignment \(a\),
\[
Q_c(a)=\sum_{b}Q_c(a,b)>0,
\tag{9}
\]
because the supplied alphabets are finite and nonempty and every summand is positive. Consequently every ordered-kernel conditional used by ID is defined and positive,
\[
Q_c(V_i=v_i\mid V_c^{(i-1)}=a)
=\frac{Q_c(V_c^{(i)}=(a,v_i))}{Q_c(V_c^{(i-1)}=a)}>0.
\tag{10}
\]
The initial kernel is strictly positive by \((1)\). Case \((2)\) passes to a marginal, which is positive by \((9)\); cases \((3)\) and \((4)\) retain the kernel; and case \((7)\) passes to a finite product of the positive terms in \((10)\). Induction down the ordinary call tree therefore shows that every reached kernel is strictly positive and every denominator guard executed in \((7)\), \((8)\), or a recursive child is discharged.

By \(\mathrm{lem:ordered\text{-}id\text{-}call\text{-}tree\text{-}finite}\), the ordinary call tree rooted at \(c_0\) is finite. Let \(h(c)\) be the height of the subtree rooted at an ordinary call \(c\). For a grammar state \(\sigma\) with \(\iota(\sigma)=c\), let \(\mathcal P(c,\sigma)\) be the conjunction of the following assertions: every complete grammar derivation rooted at \(\sigma\) projects, edge by edge and with the same case labels, to the ordinary-ID subtree rooted at \(c\); if it succeeds, then
\[
\mathcal N(\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma))
=\mathcal N(E_{\mathrm{ID}}(c)),
\tag{11}
\]
where \(E_{\mathrm{ID}}(c)\) is the expression returned by ordinary ID; and if it fails, then the propagated payload names the actual case-\((5)\) descendant, its failing pair, and its composed provenance to \(c_0\). We prove \(\mathcal P(c,\sigma)\) by induction on \(h(c)\).

If case \((1)\) applies, both systems terminate and return the same marginal by \((3)\), so \((11)\) holds. If case \((6)\) applies, both terminate and return the same Q-factor expression by \((7)\); its ratios are defined by \((10)\), so \((11)\) again holds. If case \((5)\) applies, the matching production is a failure leaf and, by the local payload premise, returns the actual call, \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal G_c,\mathcal G_c[S])\), and \(\rho(\sigma)\). The two forest subgraphs certified by that payload form a hedge for the effect at this failed scope. Shpitser--Pearl Theorem 17, recorded as \(\mathrm{lem:hedge\text{-}implies\text{-}nonidentification}\), therefore proves nonidentification at that scope. The matching transitions and failure propagation also show that ordinary ID fails from the original call \(c_0\). Its completeness theorem, recorded as \(\mathrm{lem:ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}completeness}\), gives nonidentification of the original effect. Applying the Shpitser--Pearl Theorem 19 criterion recorded in \(\mathrm{lem:hedge\text{-}criterion\text{-}subquery\text{-}scope}\) yields only the following original-query conclusion: there exist \(Y'\subseteq Y\) and \(X'\subseteq X\) for which \(P(Y'\mid\operatorname{do}(X'))\) has the relevant hedge. The retained provenance does not relabel the case-\((5)\) pair as a hedge for the full original query.

Suppose case \((2)\) applies. Its unique child has smaller height. The induction hypothesis gives transition matching and \((11)\) at \(\sigma_2\). Ordinary ID defines the parent expression to be its child expression, and the compiler does the same by \((4)\); applying \(\mathcal N\) proves \((11)\) at \(\sigma\). A child failure is propagated with provenance updated by \((2)\), so the failure assertion is also preserved. The arguments for cases \((3)\) and \((7)\) are identical, using \((5)\) and \((8)\), respectively.

Suppose case \((4)\) applies. Every district child has smaller height. Apply the induction hypothesis to each \(\sigma_{4,j}\). If a child fails, ordinary ID and the grammar both propagate that same case-\((5)\) failure, and \((2)\) gives its provenance to \(c_0\). If all children succeed, ordinary ID forms
\[
E_{\mathrm{ID}}(c)=
\sum_{V_c\setminus(Y_c\cup X_c)}
\prod_{j=1}^k E_{\mathrm{ID}}(c_{4,j}).
\tag{12}
\]
Substituting the child equalities \((11)\) into the compiler equation \((6)\), and using that \(\mathcal N\) respects finite products and marginalization, yields \((11)\) for the parent. This exhausts the seven ordered cases and completes the induction.

At \(\sigma_0\), the state embedding and the preceding induction show that every complete restricted trace is matched by the ordinary-ID call tree and uses exactly the same side conditions and ordered cases. On success,
\[
\mathcal N(\operatorname{Comp}(\sigma_0))
=\mathcal N(E_{\mathrm{ID}}(c_0)).
\tag{13}
\]
This is equality of an observed-law compiler output and the ordinary identifying functional, not a definition of the causal target. By ordinary-ID soundness, \(\mathrm{lem:id\text{-}soundness}\), whenever the right-hand side is returned, every compatible model satisfies
\[
E_{\mathrm{ID}}(c_0)(P_M(V))=P_{M,x}(Y=y)=q(M).
\tag{14}
\]
Since the checked normalization preserves evaluation, \((13)\) and \((14)\) prove the same equality for the compiled expression. On failure, the base case and propagation argument give the actual failed recursive call, its failing pair, and the corrected subquery provenance.

Because \(\mathfrak A\) was arbitrary, this proves the universally quantified abstract compiler-correctness implication. Applying it to the concrete procedure \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}\) remains conditional on an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:latent\text{-}lifting}\) that actually constructs productions, a compiler, an embedding, and a provenance map satisfying the local interface. Nothing in this proof constructs or assumes that concrete latent-lifting grammar.

added_lemmas.statement: For the ordinary seven-case recursion \(\operatorname{ID}(Y_c,X_c,Q_c,\mathcal G_c)\) on a finite ADMG with vertex set \(V_c\), suppose that the recursive edges are precisely the following: case \((2)\) replaces \(\mathcal G_c\) by the proper ancestral subgraph \(\mathcal G_c[A_c]\); case \((3)\) keeps \(\mathcal G_c\) and replaces \(X_c\) by \(X_c\cup Z_c\) for nonempty \(Z_c\subseteq V_c\setminus X_c\); case \((4)\), when the residual graph has at least two districts, creates one child with residual vertex set \(S_j\) for each such district; and case \((7)\) replaces \(\mathcal G_c\) by a proper containing-district subgraph. Then every recursive edge strictly decreases \((|V_c|,|V_c\setminus X_c|)\) in lexicographic order, and the finitely branching recursion has a finite call tree.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let
\[
r(c):=(|V_c|,|V_c\setminus X_c|)\in\mathbb N^2
\]
with lexicographic order. In case \((2)\), \(A_c=\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_c}(Y_c)\) is a proper subset of \(V_c\), so the first coordinate decreases. In case \((3)\), the graph is unchanged and
\[
V_c\setminus(X_c\cup Z_c)=(V_c\setminus X_c)\setminus Z_c,
\]
whose cardinality is strictly smaller because \(Z_c\ne\varnothing\) and \(Z_c\subseteq V_c\setminus X_c\). In case \((4)\), the nonempty districts \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\), with \(k\ge2\), partition \(V_c\setminus X_c\). Hence every \(S_j\) is a proper subset of \(V_c\setminus X_c\), and for the child intervention set \(V_c\setminus S_j\),
\[
|V_c\setminus(V_c\setminus S_j)|=|S_j|<|V_c\setminus X_c|.
\]
In case \((7)\), the containing district \(S'\) is proper in \(V_c\): if \(S'=V_c\), then \(\mathcal G_c\) would itself be a single district and the earlier ordered case \((5)\) would apply. Thus the first coordinate decreases. Cases \((1)\), \((5)\), and \((6)\) have no recursive children. The lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^2\) is well founded, so no infinite recursive path exists. Each node has finitely many children because \(V_c\) is finite. If the call tree were infinite, its root would have a child with infinitely many descendants, since it has only finitely many children. Repeating this choice would construct an infinite recursive path, contradicting the strict decrease of \(r\). Therefore the call tree is finite.

added_lemmas.statement: For an ADMG \(\mathcal G\) on \(V\), whenever the ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) algorithm returns an observed-law expression \(E_{\mathrm{ID}}\) for \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\), every causal model \(M\) represented by \(\mathcal G\) satisfies \(E_{\mathrm{ID}}(P_M(V))=q(M)\).

attestation.note: The soundness claim was checked against Theorem 38 in the cited JMLR article.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mathcal G\) be an ADMG on \(V\). If two subgraphs \(F,F'\) of \(\mathcal G\) form a hedge for \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\), then this causal effect is not identifiable from \(P(V)\) in \(\mathcal G\).

attestation.note: The hedge-to-nonidentification implication was checked against Theorem 17 in the cited JMLR article.

added_lemmas.statement: For an ADMG \(\mathcal G\) on \(V\), the effect \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) is not identifiable from \(P(V)\) if and only if \(\mathcal G\) contains a hedge for \(P(Y'=y'\mid\operatorname{do}(X'=x'))\) for some \(Y'\subseteq Y\) and \(X'\subseteq X\).

attestation.note: The existential subquery scope was checked against Theorem 19 in the cited JMLR article.

added_lemmas.statement: If the ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) algorithm fails while processing \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) in an ADMG \(\mathcal G\), then that causal effect is not identifiable from \(P(V)\) in \(\mathcal G\).

attestation.note: The failure-to-nonidentification implication was checked against Theorem 18 in the cited JMLR article.

proposed.statement: When \(W=\varnothing\) and \(\Pi\) entails strict positivity of every observed cell over \(\prod_{i\in V}\Omega_i\), the classical reduction is a deferred derived consequence of an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:latent\text{-}lifting}\), not a standalone consequence of the present construction handles. Once that resolution supplies concrete productions and a compiler satisfying the classical-ID embedding invariant, induction on the bisimilar ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) call tree proves that the restricted \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) trace uses the same ordered cases and side conditions, and that its successful compiled expression equals the ordinary ID functional up to explicit algebraic normalization, with every guard discharged by strict positivity. If the trace terminates in case \((5)\), its payload contains the actual failed recursive call, \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal G_c,\mathcal G_c[S])\), and its original-query provenance; the payload certifies a hedge for that failed query or subquery, Shpitser--Pearl Theorem 17 certifies nonidentification there, and the conclusion for the original query is only that there exist \(Y'\subseteq Y\) and \(X'\subseteq X\) such that \(P(Y'\mid\operatorname{do}(X'))\) has the relevant hedge.
proposed.justification: The abstract implication is proved for every restricted grammar, compiler, state embedding, and provenance map satisfying the stated local seven-case interface; its proof does not require an existing latent-lifting construction.
proposed.gap: The proposition itself has no remaining proof gap. Applying it to the concrete procedure requires the latent-lifting open question to construct an interface instance; that separate instantiation obligation remains open.
proposed.consumer: Any eventual concrete classical branch satisfying the local interface inherits the ordinary ID trace, normalized identifying functional, positivity-guard validity, and correctly scoped failure provenance without a second global correctness proof.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved abstract compiler-correctness argument to its explicit termination and published soundness and hedge premises, update its narrative metadata, and remove the obsolete target-local open obligation; construction of a concrete interface remains in the latent-lifting open question.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper asks for a complete support-aware analogue of the ID algorithm, \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\), for finite latent DAGs with supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and declared positive or zero observed events. Its bounded partial-trace grammar must either refute the declarations, derive a guarded formula for \(P_x(y)\), or lift a local obstruction to two exact-support rational SCMs with the same observed law while preserving \(\Omega\) and the independent latent-source architecture of \(G\). The classical branch now has a proved abstract compiler-correctness theorem: every restricted grammar instance satisfying the local seven-case embedding has the same call tree and normalized successful expression as ordinary ID, all guards follow from full support, and failures retain their actual subquery provenance. Constructing such an instance for the concrete procedure remains part of the unresolved latent-lifting question. The fully observed frontier and supported-bow separation are available, while the general independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse formula reconstruction, finite grammar, certificate syntax, and explicit complexity bounds remain open.

project_justification.fill: A completed \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) procedure must preserve \(\Omega\), exact support, functional-row provenance, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\) through recursion and certify every terminal outcome with a guarded formula, a contradiction, or a rational separating pair obeying explicit primitive and total bit bounds. On the nonfunctional full-support branch, any grammar instance satisfying the stated local embedding interface is now proved, by well-founded induction, to reproduce the seven ordered ordinary ID cases, compile the same normalized expression, discharge its ratio guards, and retain the failed subquery and original-query provenance at a hedge terminal. The remaining task is to construct a concrete interface instance as part of the latent-lifting solution; the current handles do not supply it.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the recursive seven-case ID algorithm, its soundness and completeness theorems, the theorem that a hedge implies nonidentification, and the hedge criterion with its existential subquery scope. The abstract reduction proved here uses those published results only after a direct induction establishes state-for-state compiler agreement. In particular, a case-five failure carries the actual failed call and \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal G_c,\mathcal G_c[S])\); the hedge is certified at that failed scope, and the statement transported to the original query is only that some \(Y'\subseteq Y\), \(X'\subseteq X\) subquery has the relevant hedge. The present kernel additionally requires every nonclassical countermodel pair to preserve the declared exact support, supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional rows, and independent latent-source architecture of \(G\), without requiring shared root masses. Chen and Darwiche's Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither handles arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support literals. Their constrained-identifiability work and their 2026 context-specific algorithms do not supply the present complete exact-support rational-countermodel trichotomy. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove sound-and-complete generalized identification under positivity of the observational law, not on arbitrary declared support faces. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen motivate provenance-preserving branching but do not provide the required completeness theorem. Fraser informs support consistency, Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe inform sourcewise cardinality bounds, and finite response-coordinate work informs polynomial encodings; none establishes the missing support-preserving independent-source rational lift.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The fully observed completion argument does not survive marginalization: equality of observed laws becomes a system of polynomial equalities in products of latent-source probabilities, so a local target-varying direction need not factor into independent sources, and a real separating fiber need not contain a rational point. The current trace and algorithm definitions are handles rather than a concrete production system. The abstract seven-case compiler theorem is proved, but it cannot be instantiated for the proposed procedure until the latent-lifting question constructs the required transition relation, compiler, state embedding, and provenance map. These construction and lifting tasks remain open obligations, not assumptions used by the abstract theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The support oracle, fully observed completion frontier, supported-bow formula and exact rational separating pair, and the universally quantified classical-ID compiler theorem are established. The latter proves trace matching, normalized formula agreement, positivity-guard validity, and corrected failure provenance for every abstract grammar instance satisfying the local seven-case interface; it does not construct the proposed latent grammar. The general finite grammar, concrete interface instance, terminal-certificate syntax, support-preserving independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse guarded-formula reconstruction, kill-instance audit against concrete productions, and explicit functions \(H(L)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\) with search and checking bounds remain open. A failure pair is scoped to its actual failed query or subquery, and only the existential-subquery hedge conclusion is carried back to the original query. Generic real quantifier elimination, unrestricted latent flattening, and the fully observed special case do not resolve the latent headline.

statement_notes.justification: The abstract implication is proved for every restricted grammar, compiler, state embedding, and provenance map satisfying the local seven-case interface, by well-founded induction on the ordinary ID call tree.
statement_notes.gap: No gap remains in the abstract implication. Concrete application to \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}\) still requires the latent-lifting open question to construct an interface instance.
statement_notes.consumer: A future concrete classical branch satisfying the interface immediately inherits ordinary-ID trace agreement, the same normalized identifying functional, valid positivity guards, and correctly scoped hedge provenance.
